primary_claim: Instruction fine-tuning enhances a specific attention head (L30H31) that performs copy suppression, and other heads including L13H(20-23), which together account for INSTRUCT's much better performance at the REPHRASE task compared to BASE (average logit difference 7.37 vs -1.02).
stated_future_work: Modify the prompt to include the chat template
Look at a combination of patches (pairwise) to give better insight into the incremental circuits in INSTRUCT
limitations_stated: The MLP layers (especially at L31) may play an important role in REPHRASE, though a more detailed analysis is needed to fully understand their role
The exact mechanism that suppresses "quick" AND promotes "swift" (and other synonyms) is yet to be understood
The analysis is restricted to rephrasing sentences of a specific structure; a more general analysis with a variety of sentence structures is required
A comprehensive analysis is required to understand how the models RECOGNIZE the REPHRASE command and switch on the REPHRASE circuit
The activation patching experiment here does not look at a combination of patches
quote: The average logit difference is 7.37 for INSTRUCT and -1.02 for BASE, suggesting that INSTRUCT is significantly better at rephrasing.
